text.p: Chrysler Corp. Friday priced its Plymouth Prowler at $39,000 and said the much-anticipated roadster will be in dealers' hands by the end of June or beginning of July.
The $39,000 price for the hot-rod style car includes destination charges. There are no extra-cost options. The price is at the high end of the $35,000 to $40,000 range Chrysler had previously set.
The Prowler was originally due out in March or April, but Chrysler said it took longer to work out the production processes for the new aluminum body panels.

The Prowler is now being built in small quantities at the Conner Avenue Assembly Plant in Detroit. Volume production will start later this month, said Chrysler spokesman Chris Preuss. About 2,000 Prowler's will be made in 1997.
The cars will be allocated to dealers on a formula based on volume and customer satisfaction. About 30 percent of the Chrysler-Plymouth dealer network will have Prowlers.

Standard equipment includes dual air bags, air conditioning, power windows and door locks, a 320-Watt Infinity stereo system with compact disc player, run-flat tires and a fully retractable convertible top.

"Prowler is an unprecedented combination of an outrageous yet practical design that pays homage to the rolling art of hot rods," said Martin Levine, General Manager of the Chrysler-Plymouth-Jeep-Eagle Division.
